That chart is wages, which is how much of the narrative is based on income inequality.  However much of that is an illusion of percentages. 
Between 2020 and late 2025, real wages at the 10th percentile rose 9.7% against 4.5% at the 90th. In dollars, that’s $1.34 an hour against $3.09.3 Percentage compression off a small base is not catching up. And the 2015 to 2020 dollar gains were LARGER at every percentile in the bottom half than the celebrated pandemic-era gains were.
